pr_body:
This PR does two things:
1. It allows drilling down into the `_internal/_health` API. So in addition to `GET _internal/_health`, you can also drill down into a component, like `GET _internal/_health/data` for the `data` component. And you can drill down into an individual indicator,  like `GET _internal/_health/data/ilm` for the `ilm` indicator within the `data` component.
2. It prevents `details` from being calculated or returned when calling the top-level API. This is to avoid the performance cost of calculating and sending those for each indicator at once.

Closes #84793
pr_comment: Hi @masseyke, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

review_comment: do we 404 anywhere if the component/indicator combo is invalid? ie. `data/blabla` ?

There is currently no validation (there had been at one point, but I removed it). Right now it just returns a normal response, but without the requested component or indicator. I probably ought to put that back.

I think the REST side is a bit too smart here. If a component is requested it should always compute the status IMO.

I wonder if this should have another constructor that only takes one `HealthIndicatorResult` when we drilled all the way down to one indicator? This way each constructor will do populate the necessary fields based on the use-case?

This could possibly remove the need for the other `showComponentSummary` flag in `HealthComponentResult` https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/85234/files#diff-9b325d699eee9dac56052837a367c89ec0b4613a2a28c0c4cc44e59ae6b81f99R19

What do you think?

Isn't this analogous to the top-level request? If you drill down to a component, we don't generate the status of the higher level thing (the status of the component is all that's relevant at that point). If you drill down to an indicator, we don't generate the status of the higher level thing (the status of the indicator is all that's relevant at that point).
